title: NZ Gym Routine
meta_desc: Get fit with our simple 3-day full-body gym routine for NZ beginners. Learn sets, reps, rest times, and warm-up routines to reach your goals.
intro: Starting a new gym routine can be daunting, but with a simple and effective programme, you can achieve your fitness goals. Our 3-day full-body routine is perfect for NZ beginners, and can be done at most gyms, including City Fitness, Les Mills, and Jetts. In this guide, we'll walk you through a beginner-friendly routine to get you started on your fitness journey.

sections.heading: Understanding Sets and Reps
sections.body: Before we dive into the routine, it's essential to understand the basics of sets and reps. A set is a group of repetitions of an exercise, and reps refer to the number of times you perform the exercise. For example, if you're doing 3 sets of 10 reps of bicep curls, you'll do 10 bicep curls, rest, and then repeat for a total of 3 times. This will help you build strength and endurance, and is a crucial part of any gym routine.
list: Start with lighter weights and gradually increase as you get stronger
Aim for 8-12 reps for muscle growth and 12-15 reps for muscle endurance

sections.heading: Warm-up and Cool-down Routines
sections.body: Warming up before your workout and cooling down afterwards is crucial to prevent injuries and improve flexibility. A 5-10 minute cardio warm-up, such as jogging on the treadmill or cycling, will get your blood flowing and prepare your muscles for exercise. After your workout, take 5-10 minutes to stretch and cool down, focusing on the muscles you've used. Many NZ gyms, including Anytime Fitness and Les Mills, offer group fitness classes that include warm-up and cool-down routines.
list: Include dynamic stretches like leg swings and arm circles in your warm-up
Focus on static stretches like hamstring and chest stretches in your cool-down

sections.heading: The 3-Day Full-Body Routine
sections.body: Our 3-day full-body routine is designed to work all major muscle groups, and can be done in under an hour. Day 1 focuses on chest and triceps, Day 2 on back and biceps, and Day 3 on legs and shoulders. Rest for 60-90 seconds between sets, and 120-180 seconds between exercises. You can find the equipment needed for this routine at most NZ gyms, including City Fitness and Jetts.
list: Day 1: Barbell bench press, incline dumbbell press, tricep pushdown, tricep dips
Day 2: Pull-ups, barbell rows, dumbbell bicep curls, hammer curls
Day 3: Squats, leg press, standing military press, lateral raises

sections.heading: Tips and Variations
sections.body: As you get more comfortable with the routine, you can vary the exercises and weights to keep things interesting and prevent plateaus. Consider working with a personal trainer at your gym to help you with form and technique, or try group fitness classes like those offered at Les Mills. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can also help make gym membership more affordable, with discounts of 40-70% off at participating gyms.
list: Swap barbell exercises for dumbbell exercises to target different muscle groups
Increase the weight or reps as you get stronger

sections.heading: Getting Started
sections.body: Now that you have a simple and effective 3-day full-body routine, it's time to get started. Remember to listen to your body and rest when needed, and don't be afraid to ask for help or advice from gym staff. With consistency and patience, you can achieve your fitness goals and enjoy the many benefits of regular exercise.
